events.title: Devlog 8: Chainsaws, propane, screaming crowds and dogs
events.summary: I wanted to cut through a cabin instead of going around it to find the door. That was one of the things that made the chainsaw interesting to me. The camp already had buildings, trees and people hiding inside them. A saw could change how I moved through all of that. Cut an entrance here. Drop a tree on the people over there. events.title: Devlog 7: The shotgun, the nail gun, and what an explosion is made of
events.summary: I liked the bat so much that I wanted to put some of it into the shotgun. Sending someone flying was one of my favourite things in the game. But if the shotgun just did the same thing from further away, I’d have made a second bat. I wanted another reason to pick it. That kept coming up while I was working on the weapons. events.title: Devlog 6: The bat, the machete, and what happens after the hit
events.summary: One of my favourite things in No Survivors is hitting something with the bat and watching it destroy something else. There’s a lot you can do with that idea. A person becomes a projectile. A car becomes a much bigger projectile. Eventually, you can send a tank through the camp. But I wanted those to be different stages of upgrading the weapon. events.title: Devlog 5: The lights came first, the game came second
events.summary: The Hunt in No Survivors grew out of me playing with lights. I was experimenting with glows and flashlight beams, seeing what they looked like in a dark camp. Then I started thinking about the people who would be in it. I wanted to find them somewhere in that darkness. That became a much more interesting opening to me: following music towards a campfire, or hearing someone cough inside a cabin. You know somebody is nearby, but you haven’t found them yet. events.title: Devlog 4: Everything breaks (especially my will)
events.summary: I wanted the town to come apart. I liked the idea of being able to destroy the place you were fighting in, and of that giving you more things to do with your weapons. Once I started trying it, I got a bit obsessed. Getting it to work, look right and not destroy the framerate was one of the longest fights in the project. The walls were the starting point. events.title: Devlog 3: The camp had to get bigger
events.summary: The original idea for No Survivors was a whole town. What I built first was a summer camp, with cabins, trees, campfires and people to chase. There was already quite a lot to figure out with just that. One thing I wanted was for finding people to be fun. You’re playing the bad guy, so I liked the idea of walking around looking for your next victims. I didn’t want them all standing there waiting for you. That’s why there’s music around the campfires. events.title: Devlog 2: Two days for the first prototype. Months for the demo.
events.summary: This started with a dog walk. My neighbour Lee is a graphic designer, we were both out of work, and I’d always wanted to make a game. So we said, why don’t we try? I wanted something simple. Something we could actually finish. At the time, I was thinking a couple of months. I love Vampire Survivors. There’s something about how little you need to learn before you’re enjoying it: move around, survive, get stronger, see what your weapons turn into. That seemed like a good starting point. events.title: Devlog 1 — My first game, 25 years late
events.summary: I've wanted to make a video game my whole life. I actually learned to code and became a software engineer for it, about 25 years ago. I lived in Morocco at the time and the only gaming studio there was Ubisoft. I got an interview, did a coding test, failed, and that was it. My game creation dream was over. I ended up making business software for a while, then doing an MBA and moving to startup operations. The tech left me behind and I didn't touch a line of code for 18 years. Then AI showed up.

events.title: Welcome to No Survivors. The demo is here.
events.summary: Hi, I’m Tarik. Welcome to No Survivors, and to the first post here on Steam. This is my first game. I’ve wanted to make one for years, and now there’s a demo you can actually play. Before I start getting into the story of how it all came together, I wanted to introduce the game, explain what I’m hoping to do with it, and tell you what I’ll be sharing here.
